note: First genuinely cross-model review in this phase; both assess rounds fell back to harness-native because the gateway returned HTTP 429.

dispositions.claim: Plan does not cover goal 5's PostgreSQL work; plans to keep SQLite instead.
dispositions.resolution: ESCALATED-TO-OPERATOR, NOT SELF-RESOLVED. The judge's own suggested fix named two paths: revise the goals, or add concrete PostgreSQL work. Selecting between them is a scope decision the planner must not make alone - amending goals.md to match the plan would be fitting the spec to the work. Operator chose KEEP THE GOAL on 2026-09-14. Decision 1 rewritten; changes 4/5/6 (provision-postgres-cluster, implement-postgres-daemon-backend, cut-over-deployment-to-postgres) added with falsifiable acceptance criteria.

dispositions.claim: expose-via-shared-gateway declared the DNS blocker in prose but omitted it from Depends on.
dispositions.resolution: ACCEPTED-AND-FIXED. dns-a-record-prerequisite added to the machine-readable dependency list so a scheduler cannot start certificate work before DNS resolves.

dispositions.claim: publish-fork-container-image said no workflow edit is required, then instructed adding a workflow_dispatch path.
dispositions.resolution: ACCEPTED-AND-FIXED. Genuine self-contradiction. The no-edit path (cut a v*.*.* tag) is the one implemented; workflow_dispatch is explicitly out of scope, with 'git diff touches no .github/workflows file' as an acceptance criterion.

dispositions.claim: Plan included auth changes mapping to no goal while asserting every change maps to a goal.
dispositions.resolution: ACCEPTED-AND-FIXED-AT-SOURCE. Operator ratified auth as goal 6 on 2026-09-14 and goals.md was amended. Changes 10/11 are no longer conditional; the coverage claim is now true rather than reworded. Ratification recorded with explicit scope: edge authentication only, no per-user isolation.

dispositions.claim: Runbook acceptance criterion ('a reader can reproduce the deployment') is too subjective to test.
dispositions.resolution: ACCEPTED-AND-FIXED. Replaced with five enumerated content requirements plus a fresh-namespace dry run asserting pod Ready, HTTPRoute Accepted+ResolvedRefs, Certificate Ready=True, and an HTTPS 200.
